scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

“Netherlands” is an imported map label covering about 1715–1800. It is not a single polity throughout: the Dutch Republic gave way to the Batavian Republic in 1795. The map endpoint in 1800 is not a national demise, and the VOC charter ending that year is a separate event. Imported borders are unverified.

Homes and school examples are mostly from the northern Netherlands and especially Amsterdam. Dutch overseas rule brought slavery and violence to very different communities in Asia and the Atlantic. Narrative awaits independent review.

proposedOverrides.summary: The imported Netherlands map record spans about 1715 to 1800. For most of those years the northern Netherlands was the Dutch Republic, governed through provinces and the States General; in 1795 Dutch Patriots and French troops established the Batavian Republic. Trade and skilled crafts supported Dutch town life, but wealth also came from violent colonial rule and enslaved labor in Asia and the Atlantic. Children experienced homes, schools and disease unequally. The 1800 map endpoint is not the end of the Netherlands: the Batavian state, its people and later Dutch governments continued.

identityEvidence.assessment: Imported label and interval confirmed; historic border accuracy unverified.
